label: thm:main
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: theorem:OZ
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{theorem:OZ}
There exists a continuous function $\Psi_p:\mathbb S^{d-1}\to(0,\infty)$ such that, uniformly in \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^d\) as \(\|x\|\rightarrow\infty\),
\[
 \mathbb P_p(0\leftrightarrow x, |C_0|<\infty)=
 \frac{\Psi_p(x/\|x\|)}{\|x\|^{(d-1)/2}}e^{-\xi_p(x)}(1+o_{\|x\|\rightarrow\infty}(1)),
\]
head: environment

label: lem:ld
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Take $U_i:=V_i\mathbf1_{\{V_i\le n\}}$ and
$\lambda:=\kappa n^{\beta-1}$.
By union bound and Markov inequality, for $K$ big enough one has
\begin{align*}
 \mathbb P_{\mu_\ell}(W_N>Kn)
 &\le N\mathbb P_{\mu_\ell}(V_1>n)
   +\exp\{-\lambda Kn+N\lambda m+CN\lambda^2\}\\
 &\le C e^{-c'n^\beta},
\end{align*}
Since $\mathbb E_{\mu_\ell} W_N^2\le C N^2$, the second bound follows immediately.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
There exist $K,C,c>0$, depending only on $p,d$, such that,
for every $\ell\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$, $n\ge1$ and $0\le u\le n$,
\[
 \mathbb P_p\bigl(H_\ell(C_0)\ge u,\ Kn<|C_0|<\infty\bigr)
 \le C e^{-\zeta_\ell u-cn^\beta}.
\]
head: environment

label: lem:point-plane-duality
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:point-plane-duality}
For every $\ell\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$, $\zeta_\ell\ell\in\partial\mathsf K_p$.
Consequently, every $t\in\partial\mathsf K_p$ satisfies
$t=\zeta_\ell\ell$ with $\ell=t/\|t\|$, and
\[
 \sum_{y\in\mathbb Z^d}e^{t\cdot y}G_p(y)=\infty.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $\ell$ and $0<\varepsilon<\zeta_\ell$. By \eqref{eq:master} with $v=0$,
\[
 \mathbb P_p(H_\ell(C_0)\ge u,\ |C_0|<\infty)
 \le Ce^{-(\zeta_\ell-\varepsilon)u}
      \sum_{N\ge1}\mathbb E_{\mu_\ell}[W_Ne^{-\varepsilon T_N}].
\]
Independence and \eqref{eq:moments} give
\[
 \sum_{N\ge1}\mathbb E_{\mu_\ell}[W_Ne^{-\varepsilon T_N}]
 =\frac{\mathbb E_{\mu_\ell}[V_1e^{-\varepsilon H_1}]}
        {(1-\mathbb E_{\mu_\ell}[e^{-\varepsilon H_1}])^2}<\infty,
\]
since $H_1\ge r>0$. Applying this bound to $G_p(kz)$ for
$\ell\cdot z>0$, then letting $k\to\infty$ and $\varepsilon\downarrow0$,
yields $\xi_p(z)\ge\zeta_\ell\ell\cdot z$.
For $\ell\cdot z\le0$ this is immediate. Homogeneity and continuity therefore give $$\zeta_\ell\ell\in\mathsf K_p.$$
On the other hand, \eqref{eq:coutfermeture} and the renewal decomposition imply
\[
 \sum_y e^{\zeta_\ell\ell\cdot y}G_p(y)
 \ge(1-p)^{4d}\sum_{S\text{ string}}
       e^{\zeta_\ell H_\ell(S)}w_\ell(S)
 =(1-p)^{4d}\sum_{N\ge1}1=\infty.
\]
By \eqref{eq:pointwise}, this series is finite in the interior of
$\mathsf K_p$, so $\zeta_\ell\ell\in\partial\mathsf K_p$.
Each ray from $0$ meets this boundary exactly once, proving the remaining claims.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose $t\in\partial\mathsf K_p$ with $t\cdot x=\xi_p(x)$ and set
$\ell=t/\|t\|$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:point-plane-duality},
$\zeta_\ell\ell=t$. On $\{0\leftrightarrow x\}$,
$H_\ell(C_0)\ge\ell\cdot x$, with $0<\ell\cdot x\le\|x\|$.
Thus \eqref{eq:span-volume}, with $n=\|x\|$ and $u=\ell\cdot x$,
gives \eqref{eq:main}.
head: environment

label: lem:deco
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Given all internal edges,  $C_z^D$ is in fact exactly the entire cluster if and only if its $b_D(C_z^D)$ external edges that have one endpoint in $D^c$ are closed, which openness is independent of the internal cluster. This proves \eqref{eq:extraction_locale}.
Applying this to the indicator function leads to 
\[
 \sum_{\xi_p(y-z)\ge K-a}G_p(y-z)
 \le\sum_{\xi_p(y)\ge K-a}e^{-\xi_p(y)}
 \le cK^de^{-K},
\]
head: environment

label: lem:entropy
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:entropy}
There are at most $\exp(cm\log K)$ skeletons with $m$ vertices.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Use the tree count of \cite[Lemma~4.1]{V} and multiply by at most
$(1+\lfloor\eta K\rfloor)^m$ choices of radii, still absorbed in
$\exp(cm\log K)$.
head: environment

label: lem:tree-size
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof is a routine energy-entropy argument and essentially the same as in \cite[Section~2]{CI02}. Here are the ideas :
Apply the energy--entropy argument of \cite[Section~2]{CI02}
using the energy estimate derived earlier, and Lemma~\ref{lem:entropy}.
The additional factor $\exp\{cMn/(\eta K)\}$ is absorbed by taking
$K$ large, since $\xi_p(x)\ge c_0n$.
For \eqref{eq:branches-small}, use the argument of
\cite[Section~2.4, proof of Lemma~2.2]{CIV08}:
by \eqref{eq:trunk-length}, for $\eta$ small and then $K,n$ large,
\[
 N(\mathfrak t)\ge(1-\varepsilon/2)\xi_p(x)/K.
\]
Thus $N(\mathfrak B)\ge\varepsilon\xi_p(x)/K$ implies
$N(\mathfrak T)\ge(1+\varepsilon/2)\xi_p(x)/K$, and conclude by applying \eqref{eq:tree-size}.
head: environment

label: prop:surcharge
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $n=\|x\|$ and define
\[
 Q:=\mathfrak s_t(\mathfrak t)+KN(\mathfrak B).
\]
Since $x_F\in\mathsf B_{3K}(x)$ and every trunk edge has
$\xi_p$-length at most $(1+\eta)K+a$, one has
\[
\begin{aligned}
 K\bigl(N(\mathfrak T)+1\bigr)
 &\ge \sum_{i=1}^{N(\mathfrak t)}
          \xi_p(\mathfrak t_i-\mathfrak t_{i-1})
          +KN(\mathfrak B)-(\eta K+a)N(\mathfrak t)+K\\
 &\ge t\cdot x+Q-(\eta K+a)N(\mathfrak t)-2K.
\end{aligned}
\]
Fix a sufficiently large constant $L$. For trees with
$N(\mathfrak T)\le Ln/K$, the energy estimate and
Lemma~\ref{lem:entropy} therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\mathbb P_p\bigl(E_x(M),Q\ge\varepsilon n,
                         N(\mathfrak T)\le Ln/K\bigr)\\
 &\quad\le
 (1+Ln/K)\exp\left\{-t\cdot x-\varepsilon n
       +cL\left(\eta+\frac{\log K}{K}\right)n
       +\frac{cMn}{\eta K}+cK\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Choose $\eta$ small and then $K$ large so that the two terms
proportional to $n$ in the error are at most $\varepsilon n/4$.
For sufficiently large $n$, this bound is at most
$\tfrac12 e^{-t\cdot x-\varepsilon n/2}$.

For the remaining trees, the same energy--entropy estimate gives
\[
 \mathbb P_p\bigl(E_x(M),N(\mathfrak T)>Ln/K\bigr)
 \le C\exp\left\{-\frac L2n+\frac{cMn}{\eta K}\right\}.
\]
Since $|t\cdot x|= O(n)$, uniformly in
$t\in\partial\mathsf K_p$, taking $L$ sufficiently large makes this
bound at most $\tfrac12e^{-t\cdot x-\varepsilon n/2}$.
This proves \eqref{eq:surcharge}. The last assertion follows from
$t\cdot x=\xi_p(x)-\mathfrak s_t(x)$.
head: environment

label: lem:marked
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:marked}
For $0<\delta<1/3$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:marked-deterministic}
 \#_\delta^{\mathrm{marked}}(\mathfrak t)
 \le\frac{2\mathfrak s_t(\mathfrak t)}{\delta K}.
\end{equation}
For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist $a_0,c,C>0$ and suitable
$\eta,K$ such that, if $\mathfrak s_t(x)\le a_0 n$,
\[
 \mathbb P_p(E_x(M),\#_\delta^{\mathrm{marked}}(\mathfrak t)\ge\varepsilon N(\mathfrak t))\le Ce^{-\xi_p(x)-cn}.
\]
head: environment
name: Corresponding to Lemma 4.4

title: Proof
body_md:
Use the marked-interval argument of \cite[Lemma~4.4]{V}.
For the constant in \eqref{eq:marked-deterministic}, on each forward
marked interval $[i,j)$, define
$L_{i,j}=\sum_{k=i+1}^j\xi_p(\mathfrak t_k-\mathfrak t_{k-1})$. Then
\[
 \sum_{k=i+1}^j \mathfrak s_t(\mathfrak t_k-\mathfrak t_{k-1})=L_{i,j}-t\cdot(\mathfrak t_j-\mathfrak t_i)\ge\delta L_{i,j}>\delta K(j-i),
\]
since $\mathfrak t_j-\mathfrak t_i\notin \mathcal Y_\delta^{\blacktriangleleft}$ and
$\xi_p(\mathfrak t_j-\mathfrak t_i)\le L_{i,j}$.
Sum over the disjoint forward intervals and then the backward intervals.
The probability bound follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:surcharge}
and $N(\mathfrak t)\ge c_0n/(4K)$, as in the cited proof.
head: environment

label: lem:blocked
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We use same argument as in the proof of
\cite[Section~2.7, Lemma~2.5]{CIV08}.
Let $X_i$ be the number of cone-points of the trunk blocked
by the branch $\mathfrak b_i$. By that argument,
$X_i\le c_\delta N(\mathfrak b_i)$.
Since every blocked cone-point is blocked by at least one branch,
\[\#_\delta^{\mathrm{blocked}}(\mathfrak T)\le \sum_i X_i \le c_\delta\sum_i N(\mathfrak b_i)=c_\delta N(\mathfrak B),
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:blocked-deterministic}.

For $\eta$ sufficiently small, $K$ sufficiently large, and
$n=\|x\|$ sufficiently large, \eqref{eq:trunk-length} gives
$N(\mathfrak t)\ge \xi_p(x)/(4K)$. Consequently,
\[
 \left\{\#_\delta^{\mathrm{blocked}}(\mathfrak T)
 \ge\varepsilon N(\mathfrak t)
 \right\}
 \subset
 \left\{
 N(\mathfrak B)\ge
 \frac{\varepsilon}{4c_\delta}\frac{\xi_p(x)}{K}
 \right\}.
\]
Applying \eqref{eq:branches-small} with
$\varepsilon/(4c_\delta)$ proves the probability bound.
head: environment

label: thm:tree-cones
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We combine the marked-point and blocked-point estimates of
\cite[Sections~2.6--2.8, Lemmas~2.4--2.5]{CIV08}.

Every unmarked and unblocked trunk vertex is a cone-point
of the tree. By the deterministic estimates in
Lemmas~\ref{lem:marked} and~\ref{lem:blocked},
\begin{align*}
 \#\{i:\mathfrak t_i\text{ is marked or blocked}\}
 &\le \#_\delta^{\mathrm{marked}}(\mathfrak t)
      +\#_\delta^{\mathrm{blocked}}(\mathfrak T)\\
 &\le c_\delta\bigl(
 K^{-1}\mathfrak s_t(\mathfrak t)+N(\mathfrak B)\bigr),
\end{align*}
which proves \eqref{eq:tree-cones}.

Moreover, since the trunk has $N(\mathfrak t)+1$ vertices,
\begin{align*}
 &\left\{
 \#_\delta^{\mathrm{cone}}(\mathfrak T)
 \le(1-\varepsilon)N(\mathfrak t)
 \right\}\\
 &\quad\subset
 \left\{
 \#_\delta^{\mathrm{marked}}(\mathfrak t)
 \ge\frac{\varepsilon}{2}N(\mathfrak t)
 \right\}
 \cup
 \left\{
 \#_\delta^{\mathrm{blocked}}(\mathfrak T)
 \ge\frac{\varepsilon}{2}N(\mathfrak t)
 \right\}.
\end{align*}
Choose the existing $\eta,K$ of Lemmas~\ref{lem:marked} and~\ref{lem:blocked} and take $a_0$ sufficiently small. A union bound then gives the claimed estimate whenever $\mathfrak s_t(x)\le a_0n$.

title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The exact same proof as in~
\cite[Section~2.9, Theorem~2.2]{CIV08} shows \eqref{eq:cones-thin}
Then,
\begin{align*}
 &\mathbb P_p\bigl(x\in C_0,\ |C_0|<\infty,\
       \#_\delta^{\mathrm{cone}}(C_0;0,x)\le\rho n\bigr)\\
 &\quad\le

\end{align*}
which is what we wanted.

title: Lemma
body_md:
A finite cluster containing $0,x$, with at least two cone-points
between their heights, has a unique decomposition
\[
 C=C_{\mathrm b}\sqcup C_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup C_N\sqcup C_{\mathrm f},
\]
where $N\ge 1$ and $C_{\mathrm b}\in \mathcal I_{\mathrm b}$, $C_{\mathrm f}\in \mathcal I_{\mathrm f}$, $C_i\in \mathcal I$ are translated and joined
at their marked endpoints, and
$x=X(C_{\mathrm b})+\sum_iX(C_i)+X(C_{\mathrm f})$.
Conversely every such concatenation gives one of these clusters.

label: lemma:random_walk
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{lemma:random_walk}
For $t\in\mathsf K_p$ sufficiently close to $t_0$, there exists \(C,c>0\) such that 
\[\vert r_t(x)\vert \leq Ce^{-c\|x\|^\beta} \]
with 
\[
e^{t\cdot x}G_p(x) - \sum_{n\geq 1}\sum_{a,b,y_1,...,y_n}\mathbf1_{\{a+y_1+...+y_n+b=x\}}\rho_{\mathrm b,t}(a)\rho_{\mathrm f,t}(b)\prod_{i=1}^n \mathsf p_t(y_i)=:r_t(x)
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The result follows directly from~\eqref{eq:factorisation} and the control on \(r_t(x)\) follows from Theorem~\ref{lemma:few_conepoints}
head: environment

label: proposition:tilded
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first consider $\mathsf p_t$. We consider two cases : if $\mathfrak{s}_{t_0}(y)>a_0\|y\|$, then, for
$\|t-t_0\|<a_0/2$,
\[
\mathsf p_t(y)\leq (1-p)^{-2d}e^{t\cdot y}G_p(y)\leq (1-p)^{-2d}e^{-a_0\|y\|/2}.
\]
Otherwise, since irreducible pieces have exactly two
cone-points, Theorem~\ref{lemma:few_conepoints} gives
for $\|y\|$ sufficiently large,
\[
 \mathsf p_t(y)\leq Ce^{t\cdot y-\xi_p(y)-c\|y\|^{\beta}}
 \leq Ce^{-c\|y\|^{\beta}},
\]
where we used $t\in\mathsf K_p$.

The same bounds hold for $\rho_{\mathrm b,t}$ and $\rho_{\mathrm f,t}$, and the proof is a classical OZ theory argument.
Let us define the following generating functions : 
\begin{align*}
 G(t)&:=\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}e^{t\cdot x}G_p(x),\\
 R(t)&:=\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}r_t(x),
\end{align*}
and \( H(t):=\sum_{y\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\mathsf p_t(y), ~B(t):=\sum_{y\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\rho_{\mathrm b,t}(y), ~F(t):=\sum_{y\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\rho_{\mathrm f,t}(y).\)
For any \(t\) in the interior of \(\mathsf K_p\), all of these series converge. Hence, using the decomposition above, we get the following renewal equation : 
\begin{align*}
 G(t)&=R(t)+B(t)F(t)\sum_{n\geq1}H(t)^n\\
 &=R(t)+B(t)F(t)\dfrac{H(t)}{1-H(t)}.
\end{align*}
Notice now that by estimates above, for \(t\in\partial \mathsf K_p\) close to \(t_0\), \(R(t),B(t),F(t)\) are all finite and \(G(t)=\infty\) by Lemma~\ref{lem:point-plane-duality}. Together with $H(t)\le1$, this implies that \(H(t)=1\) finishing the proof.
head: environment

label: prop:drift
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Firstly, one can use Taylor's theorem on \(H\) for vectors on the boundary of \(\partial \mathsf K_p\) since the sum \(\sum_y \|y\|^k \mathsf p_t(y)\) is uniformly bounded. Set $s=x/\|x\|$ and $m=\mathbb E_{t,0}[X_1]$.
Since every irreducible displacement has positive $t_0$ projection, one has $t_0\cdot m>0$. Consider now 
\[
 H(u)=\sum_y \mathsf p_t(y)e^{(u-t)\cdot y}.
\]
The preceding renewal argument implies that $H(u)\leq1$ in $\mathsf K_p$ near $t$, with equality on its boundary.
By Taylor near $t$,
\[
 H(u)=1+m\cdot(u-t)+O(\|u-t\|^2).
\]
In particular, if \(u\) is on the boundary one has \[m\cdot(u-t)=O(\|u-t\|^2).\]
 
Suppose $s\neq m/\|m\|$ and define $v=s-m/\|m\|$.
Direct calculation shows that $s\cdot v >0$, while $m\cdot v<0.$
For small enough $\varepsilon>0$, $(1-\varepsilon)t$ lies inside $\mathsf K_p$, and $t+\varepsilon v$ lies outside of it.
The segment joining their endpoints consequently contains a boundary point 
$$u_\varepsilon:=(1-\theta_\varepsilon)(1-\varepsilon)t
   +\theta_\varepsilon(t+\varepsilon v)$$
for some $\theta_\varepsilon\in (0,1)$.
Then, $u_\varepsilon-t$ must have a projection on $m$ that goes in the opposite direction of $m$, and that has a norm of order $\varepsilon$.
Indeed,
\begin{align*}
 m\cdot(u_\varepsilon-t)
 &=-\varepsilon\bigl((1-\theta_\varepsilon)m\cdot t
                     +\theta_\varepsilon(-m\cdot v)\bigr)\\
 &\le-\varepsilon\bigl((1-\theta_\varepsilon)c_1
                      +\theta_\varepsilon c_1\bigr)\\
 &=-c_1\varepsilon,
\end{align*}
where $c_1 := \min \{m\cdot t, -m\cdot v \}$, which is strictly positive for $t$ sufficiently close to $t_0$.
Since $u_\varepsilon\in\partial\mathsf K_p$, the preceding Taylor bound gives
$m\cdot(u_\varepsilon-t)=O(\varepsilon^2)$, a contradiction for sufficiently
small $\varepsilon>0$.

label: lemma:TLL
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. We consider two regimes :
$|N-k/c|\le k^{1/2+\varepsilon}$ and $|N-k/c|>k^{1/2+\varepsilon}$.
Write $\Sigma$ for the covariance matrix of $X_1$ and define
\[
 g_N(z)=\frac{1}{(2\pi N)^{d/2}\sqrt{\det\Sigma}}
 \exp\!\left\{-\frac{(z-Ncs)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}(z-Ncs)}{2N}\right\}.
\]
Under our moment and aperiodicity assumptions, the quantitative local
central limit theorem gives
\[
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb Z^d}|\mathbb P_0(S_N=z)-g_N(z)|
 \le C_1N^{-(d+1)/2}.
\]
In the first regime, summing this error gives
$O(k^{-d/2+\varepsilon})=o(k^{-(d-1)/2})$. A Gaussian Riemann sum,
with $v=(N-k/c)/\sqrt{k}$, therefore yields
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{|N-k/c|\le k^{1/2+\varepsilon}}\mathbb P_0(S_N=ks)
 &=\frac{C}{k^{(d-1)/2}}(1+o(1)),\\
 C&=\frac{c^{(d-3)/2}}
 {(2\pi)^{(d-1)/2}\sqrt{\det\Sigma}\sqrt{s^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}s}}>0.
\end{align*}

For the second regime, for every even integer $q\ge4$,
\begin{align*}
 \mathbb E_0\|S_N-csN\|^q&\le C_qN^{q/2},\\
 \mathbb P_0(S_N=ks)&\le\frac{C_qN^{q/2}}{|N-k/c|^q}.
\end{align*}
Summing this bound separately over $k/(2c)\le N\le2k/c$ and its
complement gives
\[
 \sum_{|N-k/c|>k^{1/2+\varepsilon}}\mathbb P_0(S_N=ks)
 \le C_q\bigl(k^{1/2+\varepsilon-q\varepsilon}+k^{1-q/2}\bigr).
\]
Taking $q$ sufficiently large makes this $o(k^{-(d-1)/2})$, which
finishes the proof.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^{d}\) and \(t\in\partial\mathsf K_p\) dual to \(x\). Firstly, thanks to Proposition~\ref{lemma:random_walk}, we have:
\begin{equation*}
e^{\xi_p(x)}G_p(x)=\sum_{a,b}\sum_{n\geq 1}\rho_{\mathrm b,t}(a)\rho_{\mathrm f,t}(b)\mathbb P_{t,0}(S_n=x-a-b) + O(e^{-c\|x\|^\beta}).
\end{equation*}
Moreover, using Proposition~\ref{proposition:tilded}, we assume (up to a negligible error) that \(\|a\|+\|b\|\leq \|x\|^{1/4}\). Therefore, this means that \(x-a-b=x+o(\sqrt{\|x\|})\), and we get that 
\[\sum_{n\geq1}\mathbb P_{t,0}(S_n=x-a-b)=\dfrac{C}{\|x\|^{\frac{d-1}{2}}}(1+o_{\|x\|}(1))\]
Overall, since the sums above over \(a,b\) converge, we can conclude that :
\[
 G_p(x)=
 \frac{\Psi_p(x/\|x\|)}{\|x\|^{(d-1)/2}}e^{-\xi_p(x)}(1+o(1)),
\]
